People confuse Free Speech and the 1st Amendment all the time. Our 1st Amendment protects our right to free speech from the government, but it does not = free speech. It did not invent that concept of free speech. It was a concept discussed under various names long before we were a country, often as being protected from government violating your ability to express views, and often from other enities. Free Speech has always just meant the right to openly express yourself without being stopped.

If I, a non-governmental entity, showed up at your house and actively prevented you from being able to express any particular view in public, you would have constitutional protection from that, and I'd go to jail for violating your right to free speech (among other things, probably).

The difference here is that their companies and websites are their own property. I can't stop you from saying something, but I can kick you out of my house if you do. Same goes for them. It's not really a freedom of speech issue, unless they have significant control over all your communication. That's actually why a lot of people have joined the call to have Google broken up into separate companies or nationalized as a public utility. One of the common claims is that Google controls so much communication and have eliminated competition, so that they are a threat to people's rights, including freedom of speech.
